assertions.name: the_filtration_basis_carries_an_EXACT_LINEAR_RELATION
assertions.source: E+ + E- = 1 holds identically in q, not merely at q_0. The k=1 operator of the filtration (the identity) is the SUM of the two k=2 operators, so {e_lambda}_{lambda |- k, k <= k_max} is overcomplete as soon as k_max >= 2. Both operators are genuine primitive idempotents (verified idempotent and mutually orthogonal), so this is a property of the corpus's basis, not of a bad choice of representatives

assertions.name: the_decomposition_is_therefore_NOT_UNIQUE
assertions.source: t*1 - t*E+ - t*E- = 0 for every t, so the coordinate vectors (x_1, x_E+, x_E-) and (x_1 + t, x_E+ - t, x_E- - t) decompose the same element, SO FAR AS the span goes. Note the sharper fact established below: for the proton's element there is no decomposition at all, because T_w lies outside the span entirely. The redundancy is real but it is not what makes 'exists x' non-redundant -- the adjunction search is

assertions.name: the_LATTICE_POINT_reading_of_N_l_is_REFUTED_measured_not_argued
assertions.source: This probe originally concluded N_l = 84 counts lattice points in the decomposition set. Measured over the k <= 3 filtration basis: rank(basis) = 4 but rank(basis | T_w) = 5 for the proton's bare 9-crossing element, so T_w is NOT in the span and the decomposition has NO solution at all. With matrix units instead the basis spans and the decomposition is UNIQUE, giving a count of 1. Neither is 84. The correct reading is in stable-atom-properties.md, a different block: 'an ILP search ADJOINING {sigma_0, sigma_1, L_+, L_-}' -- the ILP ranges over gluon ADJUNCTIONS, not decompositions. I conflated the decomposition, which fixes x from T_w, with the search, which ranges over what to adjoin

assertions.name: what_SURVIVES_is_the_overcompleteness_itself_not_its_interpretation
assertions.source: the measured facts stand: the k <= 3 filtration basis has rank 4 with nullity 2, and the two relations are exactly the completeness identities 1 = E+ + E- and 1 = sum_lambda z_lambda. The corpus's basis IS overcomplete. Withdrawn is only the inference that this overcompleteness is what N_l counts -- the span test above refutes it. Also unaffected: the Gram matrix is entrywise nonnegative, so G x >= 0 excludes nothing, and stableAt_trivial holds

description: The primitive filtration basis of def:stable-atom is linearly dependent (E+ + E- = 1 exactly; rank 4, nullity 2 over k <= 3). RETRACTED in the same file: the inference that this is what N_l = 84 counts. The proton's element is NOT in the basis span (rank 4 vs augmented rank 5), so the decomposition has no solution at all; the ILP actually ranges over gluon ADJOINDERS per stable-atom-properties.md, not over decompositions.

data.scope: (a) overcompleteness measured; lattice-point reading of N_l RETRACTED
data.correct_reading: ILP ranges over gluon ADJUNCTIONS from {sigma_0,sigma_1,L_+,L_-} (stable-atom-properties.md), not over decompositions
